cves.summary: Integer overflow in JsArrayFunctionHeapSort function used by Windows Script Engine for JScript (JScript.dll) on various Windows operating system allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a malicious web page or HTML e-mail that uses a large array index value that enables a heap-based buffer overflow attack.

mod_auth_any package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 2.1 and other operating systems does not properly escape arguments when calling other programs, which allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters.

Stack-based buffer overflow in a logging function for Windows Workstation Service (WKSSVC.DLL) allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via RPC calls that cause long entries to be written to a debug log file ("NetSetup.LOG"), as demonstrated using the NetAddAlternateComputerName API.

Microsoft Word 97, 98(J), 2000, and 2002, and Microsoft Works Suites 2001 through 2004, do not properly check the length of the "Macro names" data value, which could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a buffer overflow attack.
A malicious actor with access to the network could exploit a Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address vulnerability found in WiFiman Desktop for macOS to obtain information about the host device.

An invalid pointer dereference vulnerability exists in the vtkPNGReader::ExecuteInformation functionality of vtk 9.6. A specially crafted .png file can lead to a denial of service. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

ServiceNow has remediated a sandbox escape security issue that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. This vulnerability could enable an authenticated user with the admin role to bypass Rhino sandbox restrictions and execute arbitrary code on the underlying host operating system, potentially enabling further unintended access. 

ServiceNow deployed an update to hosted instances, and ServiceNow provided the update to our partners and self-hosted customers. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.

ServiceNow has remediated an information disclosure vulnerability that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. This vulnerability could cause a user's plaintext password to be persisted in a system table, potentially exposing that password to a user who otherwise would not be entitled to view it.

ServiceNow remediated the vulnerability through security updates that address the unintended persistence of plaintext credentials. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.
Insecure permissions in Bulk Share : Location Sender v2.1.0 (versionCode 5) allows unauthorized attackers to invoke an exported component, leading to arbitrary data access and control of data flow.

Insecure permissions in USP Ultimate Screenshot Painter versionCode 240213.009 allows unauthorized attackers to move or overwrite files in another user's private storage via supplying a crafted content URI.
Insecure permissions in the NotificationHelper component of NoNonsense Notes versionCode 72600 allows unauthorized attackers to write in another user's notes via supplying a note id.
Insecure permissions in mendhak GPSLogger versionCode 137 allows unauthorized attackers to arbitrarily manipulate the app's logging mechanism and log data.
socket.getaddrinfo() previously accepted null bytes within *host* and *port* parameters which can cause the values to be silently truncated.
An issue in the activity.LoadLinkLaterActivity component of FeedEx / Handy News Reader versionCode 116 allows attackers to force victim users into fetching a crafted URL.
Insecure permissions in Share to Clipboard v1.14.1 (versionCode 32) allows unauthorized attackers to arbitrarily overwrite another user's clipboard content.
Insecure permissions in Simple Contacts Pro versionCode 107 allow unauthorized attackers to write and read notes in another user's' note database.

Insecure permissions in the AIDL interface of ProjectMAXS MAXS Module FileRead versionCode 27 allows unauthorized attackers to arbitrarily reead files outside of the sandbox via providing an absolute path.
An issue in Shelter versionCode 445 allows attackers to register their own auth_key and execute a takeover of another user's binder service API and preference state.

A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition.

rpc.statd allows remote attackers to forward RPC calls to the local operating system via the SM_MON and SM_NOTIFY commands, which in turn could be used to remotely exploit other bugs such as in automountd.

Unknown vulnerability in the DNS intrusion detection application filter for Microsoft Internet Security and Acceleration (ISA) Server 2000 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (blocked traffic to DNS servers) via a certain type of incoming DNS request that is not properly handled.
Multiple buffer overflows in the digest authentication functionality in Pavuk 0.9.28-r2 and earlier allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.

The mod_authz_svn Apache module for Subversion 1.0.4-r1 and earlier allows remote authenticated users, with write access to the repository, to read unauthorized parts of the repository via the svn copy command.

Leon J Breedt pam-pgsql before 0.5.2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL code and bypass authentication or modify user account records by injecting SQL statements into user or password fields.

Bugzilla before 2.14 does not properly restrict access to confidential bugs, which could allow Bugzilla users to bypass viewing permissions via modified bug id parameters in (1) process_bug.cgi, (2) show_activity.cgi, (3) showvotes.cgi, (4) showdependencytree.cgi, (5) showdependencygraph.cgi, (6) showattachment.cgi, or (7) describecomponents.cgi.

Bugzilla before 2.14 does not properly escape untrusted parameters, which could allow remote attackers to conduct unauthorized activities via cross-site scripting (CSS) and possibly SQL injection attacks on (1) the product or output form variables for reports.cgi, (2) the voteon, bug_id, and user variables for showvotes.cgi, (3) an invalid email address in createaccount.cgi, (4) an invalid ID in showdependencytree.cgi, (5) invalid usernames and other fields in process_bug.cgi, and (6) error messages in buglist.cgi.

Bugzilla before 2.14 includes the username and password in URLs, which could allow attackers to gain privileges by reading the information from the web server logs, or by "shoulder-surfing" and observing the web browser's location bar.
Bugzilla before 2.14 stores user passwords in plaintext and sends password requests in an email message, which could allow attackers to gain privileges.

Internet Explorer 5.5 and earlier allows remote attackers to display a URL in the address bar that is different than the URL that is actually being displayed, which could be used in web site spoofing attacks, aka the "Web page spoofing vulnerability."

### Summary

A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow attestation verification bypass when using `gh attestation verify` with `--signer-repo` or `--signer-workflow` flags. GitHub CLI builds the certificate matcher from these flag values without escaping regex metacharacters, so a repository or workflow name is treated as a regular expression rather than a literal string. GitHub permits characters such as  `.`  in organization, repository, and workflow path names, and  `.`  is a regex wildcard, so a malicious actor can create a lookalike name that satisfies a matcher intended for a different, trusted signer.

### Details

GitHub CLI constructs a regular expression from the  `--signer-repo`  and  `--signer-workflow`  values and matches it against the signing certificate's SAN (Subject Alternative Name) during Sigstore attestation verification. The user-supplied value is interpolated into the pattern without escaping regex metacharacters, so any metacharacter permitted in a GitHub path is interpreted as regex syntax instead of a literal character.

The most practical case is  `.` , which GitHub allows in org/repo names and is a regex wildcard meaning "any single character." For example, an attacker-controlled repository named:

`github/artifact.attestations-workflows`

matches a verifier configured for the trusted signer:

`github/artifact-attestations-workflows`

because the unescaped  `.`  in the constructed pattern matches the  `-`  in the attacker's name (and any other single character at that position). This affected the `--signer-repo` and `--signer-workflow` flags but did not affect the `--repo` and `--owner` flags which include an exact string comparison.

In `v2.97.0`, the GitHub CLI escapes the user-supplied signer values before they are incorporated into the SAN matcher, so they are matched as literal strings.

### Impact

The practical impact is limited, exploitation requires the attacker to create a plausible lookalike repository name and produce valid Sigstore attestations from it. This could undermine supply chain verification for CI/CD pipelines or policy gates that use these flags to pin trust to a specific signing workflow. 

### Remediation and Mitigation

1. Upgrade `gh` to `v2.97.0` or later, which escapes signer values before matching.
2. As a workaround, use `--repo` or `--owner` flags instead of `--signer-repo` or `--signer-workflow` where applicable.
3. Manually inspect the signing certificate SAN in attestation output to confirm the signing workflow origin.

### Summary

A path traversal vulnerability has been identified in the GitHub CLI where some HTTP request URLs, REST API calls in particular, were built without properly escaping their variable path components. A value containing URL path metacharacters can alter the request path and cause `gh` to address a different resource than intended.

### Details

Not all request URLs in the codebase were built with proper escaping of their variable path components. When a component is interpolated into the path without percent encoding, and that component contains URL path metacharacters, it breaks out of its intended segment and changes the effective request path.

In `2.97.0`, request URLs are constructed in a safe manner, so a variable component can no longer escape its intended segment.

### Impact

An attacker who can control a value that flows into a request path can cause `gh` to send the request to a different API endpoint than intended. This can lead the CLI to read or act on a resource other than the one the user meant to target.

### Remediation and Mitigation

1. Upgrade `gh` to `2.97.0`.
2. Be cautious when running `gh` against untrusted repositories or inputs whose names you do not control.

cves.summary:
The `*_from_pem_callback` functions, such as `EcKey::private_key_from_pem_callback`, pass the length returned by the user's password callback to OpenSSL without checking it against the size of the buffer the callback was given. If the callback reports more bytes than the buffer holds, some OpenSSL versions read past the end of the buffer while deriving the decryption key. OpenSSL 3.x is not affected.

0.10.78 treats a returned length larger than the buffer as a failed callback.

The callbacks installed with `SslContextBuilder::set_psk_client_callback` (and its deprecated alias `set_psk_callback`), `set_psk_server_callback`, `set_cookie_generate_cb` and `set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb` each fill a `&mut [u8]` buffer and return how many bytes they wrote. The FFI trampolines handed that returned length straight to OpenSSL without checking it against the size of the buffer.

A callback that returns a length larger than its buffer makes OpenSSL read past the end of the buffer. For the cookie callbacks the cookie is sent to the peer, so adjacent memory can be disclosed over the network.

0.10.78 compares the returned length with the buffer size and treats a larger value as a callback failure.

`CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace` had the same sizing error that 0.10.79 fixed in `cipher_update` (GHSA-xv59-967r-8726); that fix missed this method. It required room for `inlen + block_size` bytes, but with the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers OpenSSL writes up to 7 more bytes when `inlen` is not a multiple of 8, past the end of `data`.

Only users of the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers are affected. `cipher_update_inplace` was added in 0.10.50, and 0.10.80 applies the corrected size check to it.

`CipherCtxRef::cipher_update`, `CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_vec` and `symm::Crypter::update` require (or allocate) `input.len() + block_size` bytes of output. With the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers (`EVP_aes_128_wrap_pad`, `EVP_aes_192_wrap_pad`, `EVP_aes_256_wrap_pad`), OpenSSL pads the input to a multiple of 8 bytes and adds an 8-byte block, so when the input length is not a multiple of 8 it writes up to 7 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer or `Vec`. If an attacker can influence the plaintext length, this is heap corruption they can partly control.

Only users of the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers are affected. 0.10.79 sizes the output for these ciphers as the input length rounded up to a multiple of 8, plus 8.

`MdCtxRef::digest_final` passed the caller's output slice to OpenSSL's `EVP_DigestFinal` without checking its length. `EVP_DigestFinal` always writes the full digest (`EVP_MD_CTX_size` bytes), so an output slice shorter than the digest is overrun. With a stack buffer this usually corrupts the stack. The overflow is reachable from safe code.

`MdCtxRef` was added in 0.10.39. 0.10.78 checks the slice length first and returns an error when the slice is too short for the digest.

`X509Ref::ocsp_responders` returns the OCSP responder URLs from a certificate's Authority Information Access extension as `OpensslString` values, which dereference to `str` without validating the bytes. OpenSSL does not require these IA5String values to be ASCII, so for a certificate with non-UTF-8 bytes in an OCSP access location, safe code ends up holding a `&str` that is not valid UTF-8, which is undefined behavior. Certificates often come from untrusted peers.

`ocsp_responders` was added in 0.9.7. 0.10.79 checks each URL and returns an error if it is not valid UTF-8.

`Deriver::derive` and `PkeyCtxRef::derive` pass the length of the caller's buffer to `EVP_PKEY_derive` and rely on OpenSSL to write no more than that. With OpenSSL 1.1.x, the X25519, X448 and HKDF-extract implementations ignore the length they are given and always write the whole result, so a buffer shorter than the shared secret or derived key is overrun. The overflow is reachable from safe code.

OpenSSL 3.x checks the length itself and is not affected. From 0.10.78, when built against OpenSSL 1.1.x or LibreSSL, both functions derive into a temporary buffer of the required size whenever the caller's buffer is too short, and copy only what fits.
Directory traversal vulnerability in ion-p.exe (aka ion-p) allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via (1) C: (drive letter) or (2) .. (dot-dot) sequences in the page parameter.

Unknown vulnerability in the NFS daemon (nfsd) in SGI IRIX 6.5.19f and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (kernel panic) via certain packets that cause XDR decoding errors, a different vulnerability than CVE-2003-0619.

Buffer overflow in WiTango Application Server and Tango 2000 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long cookie to Witango_UserReference.

Format string vulnerability in Gnu Privacy Guard (aka GnuPG or gpg) 1.05 and earlier can allow an attacker to gain privileges via format strings in the original filename that is stored in an encrypted file.

eEye SecureIIS versions 1.0.3 and earlier allows a remote attacker to bypass filtering of requests made to SecureIIS by escaping HTML characters within the request, which could allow a remote attacker to use restricted variables and perform directory traversal attacks on vulnerable programs that would otherwise be protected.

eEye SecureIIS versions 1.0.3 and earlier does not perform length checking on individual HTTP headers, which allows a remote attacker to send arbitrary length strings to IIS, contrary to an advertised feature of SecureIIS versions 1.0.3 and earlier.
Buffer overflow in dsh in dqs 3.2.7 in SuSE Linux 7.0 and earlier, and possibly other operating systems, allows local users to gain privileges via a long first command line argument.

cves.summary: Openwebmail in cPanel 5.0, when run using suid Perl, adds the directory in the SCRIPT_FILENAME environment variable to Perl's @INC include array, which allows local users to execute arbitrary code by modifying SCRIPT_FILENAME to reference a directory containing a malicious openwebmail-shared.pl executable.

Mattermost versions 11.9.x <= 11.9.1, 11.8.x <= 11.8.5, 11.7.x <= 11.7.10, 11.10.x <= 11.10.1 fail to require re-entry of the stored client secret when validating an outgoing OAuth connection, which allows an authenticated user with permission to manage outgoing OAuth connections to obtain the secret via pointing the token URL at an attacker-controlled endpoint and triggering validation.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00761
